title: Platform Academy advanced SRE curriculum draft objects
integration_notes: IDs 22-25 and 85-100 are provisional and should be reconciled before seeding live catalog data.
These objects are shaped to match the current Platform Academy Course and PlatformLab fields.
Do not publish these labs as live full labs until repository artifacts, analyzers, workspace bundles, static API exports, and cleanup scripts exist.

courses.title: Stateful Workloads and Storage Recovery
courses.description: Debug StatefulSets, PVC/PV binding, volume attachment, EBS CSI driver behavior, disruption boundaries, and recovery decisions for production Kubernetes workloads.

lessons.title: StatefulSet Identity, Ordering, and Readiness
lessons.summary: Understand stable Pod identity, ordered rollout, readiness, and why StatefulSet failure modes differ from Deployments.

lessons.title: PVC, PV, StorageClass, and Reclaim Policy
lessons.summary: Trace storage binding from claim to volume and understand capacity, access mode, zone, and reclaim decisions.

lessons.title: EBS CSI Attachment and Multi-AZ Failure Modes
lessons.summary: Debug EBS volume attach, detach, node affinity, CSI controller events, and stuck VolumeAttachment objects.

lessons.title: Stateful Recovery, Backups, and Maintenance Windows
lessons.summary: Choose repair, failover, restore, or maintenance actions with clear data-loss and downtime boundaries.

courses.title: External Secrets Operations
courses.description: Operate External Secrets Operator with AWS Secrets Manager, IRSA, refresh intervals, secret rotation, failure diagnosis, and least-privilege ownership.

lessons.title: Secret Ownership and Rotation Contracts
lessons.summary: Define which team owns secret source, sync policy, consuming workload, and rotation blast radius.

lessons.title: External Secrets Operator Resource Model
lessons.summary: Read SecretStore, ClusterSecretStore, ExternalSecret, target Secret, refresh, and status conditions.

lessons.title: AWS Secrets Manager and IRSA Integration
lessons.summary: Connect ESO service accounts to AWS Secrets Manager through least-privilege IAM trust and policy documents.

lessons.title: Sync Failures, Rotation, and Audit Evidence
lessons.summary: Debug provider errors, access denied, stale target Secrets, and rotation handoff evidence without exposing secret values.

courses.title: Service Mesh Operations
courses.description: Operate Istio or Linkerd service mesh controls for mTLS, sidecar injection, Envoy diagnostics, traffic routing, and progressive delivery safety.

lessons.title: Mesh Control Plane and Sidecar Injection
lessons.summary: Understand namespaces, injection labels, proxy lifecycle, and workload readiness after sidecar admission.

lessons.title: mTLS Policy and Identity
lessons.summary: Read PeerAuthentication, DestinationRule, service identity, and TLS mode evidence.

lessons.title: Envoy Debugging and Traffic Routing
lessons.summary: Use proxy status, config dump, routes, clusters, and endpoints to debug traffic decisions.

lessons.title: Canaries, Retries, Timeouts, and Failure Boundaries
lessons.summary: Review VirtualService or Linkerd traffic splits with explicit rollback, retry, and timeout decisions.

courses.title: Chaos, Load, and Resilience Validation
courses.description: Design controlled game days that combine k6 load tests, node disruption, SLO evidence, PDB validation, and incident response decisions.

lessons.title: Experiment Design and Blast Radius
lessons.summary: Define hypothesis, stop conditions, safety owners, and rollback before causing disruption.

lessons.title: k6 Load Profiles and SLO Evidence
lessons.summary: Build smoke, ramp, spike, and soak tests that map to user impact and error-budget evidence.

lessons.title: Node Termination, PDBs, and Capacity Recovery
lessons.summary: Validate disruption budgets, replica spread, autoscaler behavior, and recovery time under node loss.

lessons.title: Game Day Reports and Corrective Actions
lessons.summary: Turn chaos evidence into a timeline, user-impact call, follow-up list, and readiness decision.

labs.title: Debug StatefulSet EBS volume attachment
labs.scenario: A payments database StatefulSet is stuck after a node replacement because its EBS-backed volume cannot attach in the new zone.
prerequisites: No live AWS credentials required for draft mode; use the included evidence packet and mock EBS attachment records.
Optional sandbox cluster for kubectl object inspection.
Run commands from the repository root once lab artifacts are generated.
practice_steps: Record the namespace, affected ordinal, volume name, and no-live-AWS safety boundary.
Use StatefulSet identity to prove which Pod owns the stuck PVC.
Trace PVC to PV, StorageClass, zone affinity, and VolumeAttachment state.
Rule out application crash, image pull, and generic node pressure before choosing a storage fix.
Write the recovery decision: reschedule into the volume zone, detach stale attachment, restore from backup, or fail over.
Capture validation evidence and cleanup or no-runtime evidence.
expected_evidence: The stuck Pod is the stable ordinal payments-db-0, not a replaceable Deployment replica.
The PVC is bound to an EBS-backed PV with zone affinity that conflicts with the replacement node.
VolumeAttachment or CSI events show attach/detach failure rather than application startup failure.
The recovery plan names data-loss, downtime, and owner approval boundaries.
The local analyzer reports StatefulSet volume attachment analysis passed.
no_cluster_fallback: Use cluster-snapshot.yaml, volume-events.txt, and mock-ebs-volumes.json as the evidence source.
Write recovery-decision.md without making any AWS or cluster mutation.
cluster_workspace_commands: Use only a disposable sandbox context.
worksheet_prompts: Record context, namespace, affected ordinal, PVC, PV, and no-live-AWS safety boundary.
Paste StatefulSet, Pod, PVC, PV, StorageClass, and VolumeAttachment evidence.
Explain why this is not an app crash, image pull, or generic node-pressure incident.
Identify the zone or stale attachment conflict and the owner who can approve remediation.
Write the recovery decision with data-loss, downtime, rollback, and backup boundaries.
Capture analyzer output, validation output, and cleanup or fallback evidence.
rubric: Preserves the no-live-AWS and data-safety boundary before recovery decisions.
Traces StatefulSet ordinal identity through PVC, PV, StorageClass, and VolumeAttachment.
Uses CSI and attach/detach evidence rather than generic Pod restart assumptions.
Names zone affinity or stale attachment as the failure mode with supporting evidence.
Chooses a recovery path with explicit data-loss, downtime, owner approval, and rollback notes.
Saves analyzer output, validation output, and cleanup or fallback evidence.
validation_checks: StatefulSet ordinal and PVC owner identified
PV, StorageClass, and zone evidence captured
VolumeAttachment or CSI failure evidence captured
Recovery decision written with data-loss and downtime boundary
checklist: Trace Pod ordinal to PVC and PV before changing anything.
Inspect StorageClass, reclaim policy, node affinity, and VolumeAttachment.
Use CSI events to separate attach failure from app failure.
Write recovery decisions with backup, owner, rollback, and downtime boundaries.

labs.title: Integrate External Secrets with AWS Secrets Manager
labs.scenario: A checkout workload expects a Kubernetes Secret from External Secrets Operator, but sync is failing after a Secrets Manager rotation.
prerequisites: No real secret values or AWS credentials required; use mock provider responses and IAM documents.
Optional sandbox cluster with ESO CRDs installed.
Never paste secret values into worksheet evidence.
practice_steps: Record namespace, target Secret name, provider secret ARN, and no-secret-value evidence boundary.
Read ExternalSecret status and ESO controller logs before changing IAM or manifests.
Trace SecretStore service account to IRSA trust subject and Secrets Manager permissions.
Identify whether the failure is remote key mismatch, IAM denial, stale refresh, or target Secret ownership.
Write the least-privilege fix and rotation validation plan without exposing secret data.
Capture validation output and cleanup or no-runtime evidence.
expected_evidence: ExternalSecret status shows sync failure or stale target Secret condition.
Controller logs or mock provider transcript show AccessDenied or missing remote key evidence.
IRSA trust policy subject matches the ESO service account and namespace.
Least-privilege policy allows only the required Secrets Manager ARN and read actions.
The local analyzer reports External Secrets integration analysis passed.
no_cluster_fallback: Use externalsecret.yaml, secretstore.yaml, controller-log.txt, provider-response.json, and IAM documents as evidence.
Write rotation-note.md and least-privilege-review.md without creating real secrets.

worksheet_prompts: Record namespace, target Secret, provider secret ARN, service account, and no-secret-value boundary.
Paste ExternalSecret condition and ESO controller-log evidence without secret values.
Paste SecretStore serviceAccountRef, IRSA trust subject, and policy scope evidence.
Explain whether the failure is IAM, remote key, refresh, or target ownership.
Write the least-privilege and rotation validation note.
Capture analyzer output, validation output, and cleanup or fallback evidence.
rubric: Preserves the no-secret-value evidence boundary.
Reads ExternalSecret status and ESO controller logs before changing IAM.
Traces SecretStore service account to IRSA trust and least-privilege policy.
Separates IAM denial, remote key mismatch, stale refresh, and target Secret ownership evidence.
Writes a rotation validation plan that proves sync without leaking values.
Saves analyzer output, validation output, and cleanup or fallback evidence.
validation_checks: Controller log or mock provider evidence captured
SecretStore service account and IRSA trust reviewed
checklist: Inspect ExternalSecret status and controller logs before editing IAM.
Map SecretStore identity to IRSA trust and AWS permissions.
Validate remoteRef key, property, refresh interval, and target Secret ownership.

labs.title: Debug mesh mTLS and traffic routing
labs.scenario: A checkout service was onboarded to a service mesh and now receives intermittent 503 responses after sidecar injection and mTLS policy changes.
prerequisites: No production mesh required; use local manifests and proxy evidence in draft mode.
Optional sandbox mesh such as Istio demo profile or Linkerd edge install.
Run commands from the repository root once lab artifacts are generated.
practice_steps: Record mesh type, namespace injection label, affected workload, and rollback boundary.
Prove whether both client and server have sidecars before blaming the application.
Read PeerAuthentication or Linkerd identity policy and identify mTLS mode.
Trace route, subset, DestinationRule, endpoints, and weight evidence.
Explain whether the 503 is caused by mTLS mismatch, missing sidecar, bad subset labels, or traffic split drift.
Write the smallest source-manifest fix and rollback command.
expected_evidence: Namespace and Pod labels show whether sidecar injection is enabled and applied.
mTLS policy evidence shows STRICT mode or equivalent identity requirement.
DestinationRule or traffic split references a subset that does not match ready Pods.
Proxy evidence shows route or cluster mismatch supporting the failure mode.
The local analyzer reports service mesh routing analysis passed.
no_cluster_fallback: Use mesh-manifests.yaml, proxy-evidence.txt, namespace-labels.txt, and traffic-split-report.txt as the evidence source.
Write routing-decision.md without installing a mesh.
cluster_workspace_commands: Use only a disposable sandbox mesh.
Verify mesh evidence and routing decision: ./validate.sh --cluster
worksheet_prompts: Record mesh type, namespace, injection state, affected workload, and rollback boundary.
Paste sidecar injection and workload readiness evidence.
Paste mTLS policy, service identity, and TLS mode evidence.
Paste route, subset, endpoint, and traffic weight evidence.
Classify the failure as mTLS mismatch, missing sidecar, bad subset, or traffic split drift.
Write the source-manifest fix, rollback command, analyzer output, and cleanup evidence.
rubric: Preserves a rollback boundary before changing mesh policy.
Proves sidecar injection state for client and server workloads.
Reads mTLS mode and identity evidence before changing traffic policy.
Traces route, subset, DestinationRule, endpoint, and weight evidence.
Classifies the mesh failure mode with proxy or manifest evidence.
Saves source-manifest fix, rollback, analyzer output, validation output, and cleanup evidence.

Endpoint and traffic weight evidence captured
checklist: Check injection before debugging app code.

Trace proxy routes, clusters, subsets, endpoints, and weights.
Patch source manifests and keep a rollback path.

labs.title: Run k6 load and node termination game day
labs.scenario: A checkout API must prove it can keep its SLO during load while one worker node is terminated or drained.
prerequisites: No production cluster disruption allowed; use local simulator or disposable sandbox only.
k6 installed locally or use the included summary transcript.
Define stop conditions before running any disruption.
practice_steps: Record hypothesis, blast radius, owner, stop condition, and no-production-disruption boundary.
Run or inspect the k6 baseline and capture p95 latency, error rate, and throughput.
Inspect replicas, PDB, topology spread, and node placement before disruption.
Simulate or dry-run node termination and capture scheduling/recovery evidence.
Compare during-disruption k6 results with SLO threshold and stop condition.
Write game day report with pass/fail decision, corrective actions, and follow-up owners.
expected_evidence: The experiment plan names hypothesis, blast radius, stop condition, and rollback owner.
Baseline k6 summary captures p95 latency, request rate, and error rate.
